summary.one_line: A small Bikaner papad maker (FY26 revenue Rs 33.5 cr, PAT Rs 5.2 cr) whose reported profits have barely turned into cash: inventory is about 75% of annual sales. It has no real moat, runs parallel snack businesses on the promoter side, and nearly a third of the fresh money goes to paying down a revolving bank line. Avoid.
bull_points: Reported profitability has improved sharply: operating EBITDA margin rose from 12.58% in FY24 to 25.16% in FY26 and PAT from Rs 210.76 lakh to Rs 521.26 lakh, helped by a richer machine-made and modern-trade mix (S1).

Channel mix is shifting towards modern trade, which grew from Rs 685.44 lakh (26.09%) in FY24 to Rs 1,366.15 lakh (40.74%) in FY26. Customer concentration also fell: the top 10 customers were 45.94% of FY26 revenue versus 69.25% in FY25 (S1).
Rice papad (khichiya) capacity is genuinely full at 93.15% utilisation in FY26, so the Bachhasar khichiya plant answers a real bottleneck rather than being speculative capacity (S1).
Almost all of the issue is fresh capital: 25,72,800 fresh shares against an OFS of just 2,30,400 shares (about Rs 1.66 cr), and promoters are not selling (S1, S5).
bear_points: Profits are not converting to cash. Cumulative operating cash flow over FY24-FY26 was Rs 22.63 lakh against cumulative PAT of Rs 1,204.46 lakh, because inventory rose from Rs 1,468.97 lakh to Rs 2,498.61 lakh on FY26 revenue of Rs 3,353.48 lakh (S1).
Packing-material stock of Rs 816.06 lakh at March 2026 compares with packing material consumed of only Rs 151.33 lakh in FY26, which is more than five years of usage on the books (S1).

There is no moat. The RHP itself says entry barriers in papad are 'relatively low', the 'Vishal' trademark applications are opposed by third parties, and the company is roughly 0.3% of a market Frost & Sullivan projected at INR 103 billion for FY26 (S1, S12).

Rs 580.26 lakh (about 31% of the fresh issue at the upper band) repays an Axis Bank cash-credit line that is repayable on demand. Total borrowings actually rose from Rs 998.56 lakh at March 2026 to Rs 1,378.64 lakh by August 31, 2026 (S1).

The MD is a director and shareholder of Bhujialalji Pvt Ltd, a Bikaner snacks company 49% owned by Bikaji Foods since 2023, and of Kachoree Club Pvt Ltd. Both sit in the same food-processing space, and the company sells goods to Bhujialalji (S1, S13).
watch_points: Final subscription split. The QIB quota is only 32,000 shares and there is no anchor book, so demand will be almost entirely individual and NII money (S1, S2).
India Customer Insight Fund keeps 20,89,188 shares (22.24% post-issue) that are NOT locked in, bought at an average cost of Rs 43.11, so they could be sold from listing day (S1).
Resolution of the Rs 276.84 lakh income-tax demand under section 147, which is under appeal with CIT(A) and equals about 53% of FY26 PAT (S1).
Whether Bachhasar statutory approvals (not yet applied for as of the RHP) and orders (none placed) start on the November 2026 to January 2028 schedule (S1).
The FY27 inventory and operating-cash-flow trend in the first post-listing results: the single number that would change this call (S1).

reasoning: Earnings quality is the deciding problem. Three years of restated PAT totalling Rs 1,204.46 lakh produced only Rs 22.63 lakh of operating cash flow. FY26 inventory of Rs 2,498.61 lakh is about 272 days of revenue, including packing material worth more than five years of consumption. Until cash flow confirms the margins, the 25% EBITDA margin cannot be taken at face value (S1).

The use of money does not change the business quickly. Rs 580.26 lakh goes to a revolving cash-credit line that was re-drawn to Rs 1,073.70 lakh by August 2026. The Rs 790 lakh plant is budgeted ex-GST, has no orders placed and no approvals applied for, sits on land leased from the promoter at Rs 1.80 lakh a month, and only starts commercially in January 2028 (S1).

There is no moat. The company is a regional papad brand house with about half its sales in Rajasthan (50.42%), no contracts with general-trade buyers, and a 'fixed pricing structure'. Its biggest brand name ('Vishal') is not registered and is opposed. Lijjat alone is reported at about Rs 1,600 cr of revenue against Papadmalji's Rs 33.5 cr (S1, S14).

Governance flags add up. The promoter runs parallel snack companies, one of them an associate of listed rival Bikaji. The RHP has several internal contradictions (brand revenue, handmade-papad revenue, customer concentration and inventory figures differ between chapters), there have been repeated ROC, EPF and TDS filing delays, and the board is new: both independents and the CFO were appointed in 2025 and the 19-year-old daughter is a promoter-director (S1, S13).

Growth has already slowed. Revenue grew 20.85% in FY25 but only 5.62% in FY26, and machine-made papad capacity was only 68.70% utilised. Management has given no quantified outlook beyond the plant rationale (S1).

subsections.title: What it makes and how it earns

blocks.text: Papadmalji Agro Foods is a Bikaner, Rajasthan papad manufacturer. The business began in 2012 as Vishal Namkeen Bhandar, a sole proprietorship of promoter Jai Agarwal, and was taken over by the company (incorporated December 19, 2017) under a slump-sale business transfer agreement dated February 17, 2018 (S1). It makes hand-made papads, machine-made papads, machine-made ready-to-fry papads, rice papads (khichiya), vrat-special papads and moongodi. It also does white-label hand-made papads for other brand owners and trades cereal pellets under its own brand (S1).

Revenue is earned by selling packaged product under five brands. Zhakaas (rice papads, vrat papads, ready-to-fry, pellets, moongodi) goes through general trade, modern trade and quick commerce. Vishal (hand-made) goes through general trade and a merchant exporter. Rozana (machine-made) goes mainly to modern trade and quick commerce. Diamond is hand-made for select general-trade markets, and Papadmalji is a direct-to-consumer brand sold on the company's own site (S1). The company does not export directly: Middle East volumes are sold within India to an independent merchant exporter on purchase orders (S1). The RHP describes a 'fixed pricing structure across various product categories', so pricing power rests on brand familiarity rather than contracts (S1).

blocks.caption: Revenue by business vertical, Rs lakh (RHP, Our Business)

blocks.text: Look closely at the trading line. FY25 revenue was inflated by Rs 218.96 lakh of groundnut trading (discontinued from October 24, 2024) and Rs 133.94 lakh of 'others' (RNR paddy and raw rice trading, discontinued from May 2025) (S1). Stripping trading out, the core manufactured business grew from about Rs 2,549 lakh in FY24 to Rs 2,728 lakh in FY25 and Rs 3,232 lakh in FY26. That is the 'finished goods' line in the revenue note (S1).

The RHP's own revenue splits do not reconcile across chapters. FY26 hand-made papad revenue is Rs 1,386.04 lakh in one risk factor but Rs 1,051.60 lakh in another and in the business chapter. The 'Papadmalji' brand is Rs 113.9 lakh in one table and Rs 0.82 lakh in another. Figures above use the business-chapter tables (S1).

subsections.title: Plants, capacity and the Batara-Batari model

blocks.text: The company runs two FSSAI-licensed units in Bikaner plus a maintenance store, and all three premises are rented (S1). The Gharsisar unit (15,480 sq ft, ISO 22000:2018 certified, also the registered office) is owned by the promoter-MD and rented at Rs 1.30 lakh per month for 33 months from April 2025. The Karni unit (4,800 sq ft) is rented from a third party at Rs 31,500 per month (S1). Employees numbered 118 at FY26 (S1).

Hand-made papads are produced outside the factory through the Batara-Batari system. Contractors (Bataras) supervise women (Bataris) who roll papads at home. The company supplies dough in stainless-steel containers and besan in PP bags, which stay company property, then inspects the dried papads at the Gharsisar unit and pays Bataras twice a month for accepted quantities (S1). This is the same outsourced home-rolling model Lijjat uses at scale. It keeps fixed costs low, but it means the company's largest single product line is made outside its direct supervision (S1, S14).

blocks.caption: Installed capacity and utilisation (kg per year, RHP operational KPIs)

blocks.text: The capacity picture matters for the IPO story. Only khichiya is near full. Machine-made papad has run at under 70% for three years and moongodi at under a quarter of capacity, so the new plant's case rests on the rice papad line alone (S1).

subsections.title: Customers, suppliers and the distribution chain

blocks.text: Raw materials (urad and moong dal, flours, spices, edible oil, sugar, packaging) are bought mostly within Rajasthan on purchase orders or 'as needed', with no short- or long-term supply agreements (S1). For khichiya, poha and papad khar come from Gujarat, packaging from Delhi-NCR, and pulses, salt and cartons from Bikaner (S1). Material cost was 58.54% of total expenses in FY26 (S1).

blocks.caption: Customer and supplier concentration (share of revenue / purchases)

blocks.text: Selling runs through 76 distributors and 30 wholesalers, reaching 8,710 retail outlets as of March 31, 2026, up from 55 distributors and 15 wholesalers in FY24 (S1). Distributor reach is heavily Rajasthan-weighted: 55 of the 76 distributors and 5,000 of the 7,470 distributor-served outlets are there (S1). General trade is 57.91% of FY26 revenue and runs on phone orders with no order book or binding contracts (S1). Modern trade (40.74%) and quick commerce (1.07%) run on purchase orders. D2C is negligible at Rs 0.25 lakh (S1).

The RHP names no customers. The FY25 drop in trading and white-label revenue, plus modern-trade growth, largely explains why top-10 concentration fell from 69% to 46%. Note too that the risk-factor text gives FY26 top-10 concentration as 40.53% while its own table shows 45.94% (S1).

The RHP's industry chapter covers Indian snacks and food processing broadly. It cites an India snacks market of INR 48,543.1 crore in 2025 growing at an 8.91% CAGR over 2026-2034, but gives no papad-specific market size or share data (S1). For papad specifically, the best independent figures found are from Frost & Sullivan's 2022 report prepared for Bikaji Foods (S12).

blocks.caption: Indian papad market (Frost & Sullivan, 2022, prepared for Bikaji)

blocks.text: Against those figures, Papadmalji's FY26 revenue of Rs 33.53 crore is roughly 0.3% of the projected FY26 total papad market and about 0.9% of the projected organised segment (analyst's calculation from S1 and S12). The market is large and growing steadily, but it is two-thirds unorganised, which cuts both ways. There is room to formalise share, but a vast pool of low-cost local producers also caps pricing (S12).

Frost & Sullivan names Lijjat, Bikaji, Agarwal 420 and Shree Ram papad as the organised players, with the rest of the market dominated by unorganised makers and women's self-help groups (S12). Lijjat, the cooperative leader, is reported at about Rs 1,600 crore of annual revenue with 45,000 women rollers, roughly 48 times Papadmalji's size (S14). Bikaji Foods, listed and also Bikaner-based, calls itself the second-largest maker of hand-made papad in India (S12).

The RHP's own risk factor is candid. It describes the papad industry as fragmented, with 'entry barriers ... relatively low due to limited capital investment requirements, local availability of raw materials, and access to distribution channels', and competition 'based primarily on pricing, brand recognition, product quality and distribution reach' (S1). It also warns that larger food companies with bigger distribution may push harder into papads (S1).

items: Lijjat (cooperative, unlisted): national leader; same home-rolling model at far larger scale (S14).
Bikaji Foods (listed): Bikaner neighbour; hand-made papad is a category within a much larger snacks business (S12).
Agarwal 420 and Shree Ram papad: organised regional brands named by Frost & Sullivan (S12).
Unorganised Bikaner and Rajasthan papad makers: the price-setters in general trade, where Papadmalji makes 58% of its sales (S1, S12).

blocks.text: No, on the evidence in the offer document. The company makes no market-share claim, no import-substitution claim and no technology or regulatory-barrier claim. Its stated strengths are distribution reach, brands and traditional recipes (S1). Those are real operating assets but not defensible ones. The three core brands (Zhakaas, Vishal, Rozana) are 88.7% of FY26 revenue, yet the two 'Vishal' device-mark applications (filed in 2016) are opposed by third parties. The new Papadmalji, Rozana-oil and Diamond logos are only 'ready for examination' (S1). Registered protection currently extends to the 'PAPADMALJI'S ROZANA' word mark and a Papadmalji device mark (S1).

The most defensible element is regional brand familiarity in Rajasthan, Haryana and Assam, which together gave 71.98% of FY26 revenue (S1). The margin jump from 12.58% to 25.16% EBITDA in two years is presented as mix and operating leverage (S1). In a low-barrier, price-competitive category, a margin that high invites competition, and it has not yet been validated by cash flow (see Financials).
Plainly: no genuine moat. This is a regional papad brand house in a category where the market leader is almost 50 times its size and the RHP itself says barriers to entry are low (S1, S14).

blocks.caption: Restated profit and loss, Rs lakh (RHP)

blocks.text: The story in the P&L is margin expansion, not volume. Revenue grew at a modest pace (about 13% CAGR over two years, 5.62% in FY26), while gross margin rose about 13 percentage points. The cause is lower material cost relative to sales plus a much smaller trading line (analyst's calculation from S1). PBT more than tripled from Rs 213.24 lakh to Rs 724.22 lakh (S1).

PAT growth slowed to 10.33% in FY26 because tax normalised. FY24 and FY25 carried no current tax, as brought-forward losses of Rs 184.51 lakh and Rs 453.82 lakh were set off, while FY26 bore Rs 178.61 lakh of current tax plus Rs 20.69 lakh for earlier years (S1). FY26 PAT is therefore the first 'clean' tax year. The restatement adjustments to audited profit were small (gratuity only) (S1).

subsections.title: Balance sheet and the cash-flow problem

blocks.caption: Balance sheet and cash flow, Rs lakh (RHP)

blocks.text: This is the single biggest red flag in the filing. Over FY24-FY26 the company reported PAT of Rs 1,204.46 lakh but generated just Rs 22.63 lakh of operating cash (analyst's sum from S1). Nearly all the difference went into inventory, which added Rs 1,619.37 lakh across the three years (S1). At FY26, inventory of Rs 2,498.61 lakh equals roughly 272 days of revenue. Cash on hand was Rs 2.35 lakh, and the business runs on a bank cash-credit line and promoter loans (S1).

The inventory note is stranger still. Packing-material inventory was Rs 816.06 lakh at March 2026 against only Rs 151.33 lakh of packing material consumed in the year. At March 2025 it was Rs 743.40 lakh against Rs 27.94 lakh consumed (S1). Raw-material stock of Rs 1,235.48 lakh is close to a full year's raw-material consumption of Rs 1,387.78 lakh, even though pulses and spices are bought locally with no supply contracts (S1). The RHP gives no explanation for holding years of packaging stock. Its own working-capital table puts FY26 inventory at Rs 2,416.62 lakh, not the Rs 2,498.61 lakh in the balance sheet (S1).
Cash conversion does not support the reported margins. Until inventory falls and operating cash flow tracks PAT, the FY26 profit of Rs 521 lakh should be treated as unproven (S1).

subsections.title: Does the trend support the growth story?

blocks.text: Only partly. Profitability ratios look excellent on paper: the RHP's KPIs show ROE of 38.51% and ROCE of 46.47% for FY26 (S1). Revenue momentum, though, faded to 5.62% in FY26, trading income is being wound down, and the machine-made papad plant still has about 30% spare capacity (S1).

items: Receivables are rising: turnover fell from 23.92x in FY24 to 10.56x in FY26, which the company attributes to longer modern-trade credit terms (S1).
Bad debts written off jumped to Rs 29.91 lakh in FY26 from Rs 0.15 lakh in FY25 (S1).
Rent rose to Rs 24.87 lakh in FY26 from Rs 5.43 lakh, including Rs 19.27 lakh paid to the promoter. The new Bachhasar lease adds Rs 1.80 lakh a month (S1).
Contractual charges (largely Batara payments) rose to Rs 273.78 lakh from Rs 191.36 lakh (S1).
Contingent liability: an income-tax demand of Rs 276.84 lakh under section 147 (notice dated March 30, 2024) is under appeal and not provided for (S1).

blocks.text: Secondary sources disagree with the RHP on basic items. One summary lists the issue on BSE SME with FY24 revenue of 'Rs 262.88 crore' and objects that do not match the RHP (S8). Another quotes a debt/equity of 1.08x (S7). This report uses the RHP's restated figures throughout (S1).

sections.title: Issue details and objects of the issue

blocks.caption: Offer structure (RHP; price band per company announcement)
rows: Sept 29 - Oct 1, 2026; allotment Oct 5; listing Oct 7 (NSE Emerge)
28,03,200 shares (about Rs 20.18 cr at upper band)
2,30,400 shares by India Customer Insight Fund (about Rs 1.66 cr)

blocks.text: The OFS is small (about 8% of the offer), so roughly 92% of the money raised goes to the company (S1, S5). Chittorgarh's page shows the fresh issue as 24,28,800 shares, which conflicts with the 25,72,800 in the RHP. The RHP figure is used here (S1, S2). The price band was announced on September 28, 2026, the day before opening (S5, S15).

The OFS seller, India Customer Insight Fund (a SEBI Category II AIF), invested at Rs 388 per share across five private placements in 2018-2020. After the 8:1 bonus in September 2025 its average cost is Rs 43.11 per share, against about Rs 1.10 for the promoters (S1).

blocks.caption: Use of net proceeds, Rs lakh (RHP)
rows: Bachhasar plant: building and civil works
Bachhasar plant: rice-papad and packaging machinery
Repay / prepay Axis Bank cash credit
[not fixed; capped at 15% of gross or Rs 10 cr]

blocks.text: At the upper band the fresh issue raises about Rs 1,852 lakh. Capex and debt take Rs 1,370.26 lakh, leaving about Rs 482 lakh for issue expenses and general corporate purposes (analyst's calculation from S1). So about 43% of fresh money goes to the plant, about 31% to repaying a working-capital line, and the balance to expenses and GCP (analyst's calculation from S1).

The debt being repaid is an Axis Bank SBB cash-credit facility (sanction Rs 1,200 lakh, outstanding Rs 1,073.70 lakh at August 31, 2026). It is secured on stock and debtors plus the promoters' personal properties and guaranteed by both promoters (S1). Because it is a revolving line, repaying it frees borrowing room rather than permanently deleveraging, and the company has already drawn more since March: total borrowings were Rs 1,378.64 lakh at August 31, 2026 versus Rs 998.56 lakh at March 31, 2026 (S1). The repayment also releases the promoters' personal guarantees and collateral to that extent.

The plant sits on a 45,000 sq ft converted industrial plot at Khasra No. 394/4, Village Bachhasar. The land is owned by promoter Jai Agarwal and leased to the company for 15 years from February 1, 2026 at Rs 1.80 lakh a month, and 'already owned by the Promoter' is listed as a reason for choosing the site (S1). The plant will take over khichiya production from the rented Karni unit, which will close. It will add 5-inch and 7-inch rice papads under Zhakaas and mini machine-made papads under Rozana (S1).

items: No orders have been placed for machinery, the building or electricals, and quotations are valid only to December 19, 2026 (S1).
None of the five required approvals (pollution consent to establish and operate, fire NOC, factory licence, FSSAI) had been applied for as of the RHP (S1).
Schedule: approvals Nov 2026 - Feb 2027; civil works Dec 2026 - Nov 2027; machinery Sept - Dec 2027; commercial start January 2028 (S1).
Costs are budgeted ex-GST. The quotations carry GST of Rs 79.31 lakh (building), Rs 50.67 lakh (machinery) and Rs 3.40 lakh (solar), about Rs 133 lakh in all, outside the Rs 790 lakh (S1).
Costs of shifting the other two units to Bachhasar, and utilities, are to come from internal accruals and are not quantified (S1).
The company says it is eligible for a capital subsidy of up to 50% of capital investment, capped at Rs 1.50 crore and paid at 5% a year over 10 years (S1).

blocks.text: The project is sensible in concept, since khichiya is at 93% utilisation. But it will not contribute before FY28, it depends on approvals not yet sought, it may need more money than budgeted, and it deepens the company's dependence on promoter-owned property (S1).

Jai Agarwal (43, B.Com) is Chairman and MD. He founded the predecessor proprietorship in 2012 and the RHP credits him with more than 13 years in papad, namkeen and ethnic snacks (S1). His wife Prem Lata Agarwal (46, MA Sociology) is Whole-time Director and heads HR, and their daughter Aanya Agarwal (19, a student) was made a non-executive director in July 2025 and a promoter in January 2026 (S1). The two independent directors, CA Prafful Bhojak (36) and CA Prasad Ramanuj Heda (30), joined in May 2025. The CFO (Priya Mungia, CA, about two years' post-qualification experience) and Company Secretary were appointed on May 5, 2025 (S1).

blocks.caption: Shareholding and lock-in (RHP)
rows: 16.5 lakh sh 3 yrs; 9.75 lakh 2 yrs; 9.75 lakh 1 yr
2.50 lakh sh 3 yrs; 1.54 lakh 2 yrs; 1.54 lakh 1 yr

blocks.text: Under the SME lock-in rules as applied in the RHP, 20.23% of post-issue capital (the minimum promoters' contribution) is locked for three years. The promoters' remaining shares are split into halves locked for two years and one year (S1). The notable gap is India Customer Insight Fund. As an AIF its residual 22.24% stake is exempt from lock-in under Regulation 239(c), so a large holder bought at Rs 43.11 can sell from day one (S1). Promoters hold 44.28% after the issue (S1).

The promoters run other snack businesses. Jai Agarwal is a director and shareholder of Bhujialalji Pvt Ltd (namkeen and sweets) and Kachoree Club Pvt Ltd (kachori and beverages), and a director of Better for You Foods Pvt Ltd and Insanely Good Foods Pvt Ltd. Prem Lata Agarwal is a director of Bhujialalji (S1). The RHP concedes these are 'engaged in the same industry' but argues they serve distinct product segments. The promoters undertake that entities they majority-control will not enter the company's line of business after listing without shareholder approval (S1).

The Bhujialalji link deserves attention. In July 2023 Bikaji Foods, a listed Bikaner rival and self-described second-largest hand-made papad maker, bought 49% of Bhujialalji for Rs 5.10 crore, with Jai Agarwal quoted as its promoter (S13, S12). The promoter's time and loyalties are therefore split with a business in which a direct papad competitor is the largest outside shareholder. Because the undertaking above covers only majority-controlled entities, it is weaker for companies like this.

blocks.caption: Main related-party transactions, Rs lakh (restated note 30)

blocks.text: Most of these are routine for a promoter-funded SME. The promoters have used personal loans to fund working capital and have pledged personal property to the bank (S1). The concerns are structural rather than any single transaction: rent to the promoter on two sites, sales to a promoter company part-owned by a competitor, and year-end receivables from the promoters themselves of Rs 8.27 lakh (Jai) and Rs 19.80 lakh (Prem Lata) (S1). Approved remuneration ceilings of up to Rs 5 lakh a month for the MD and Rs 4 lakh a month for the WTD are more than double the Rs 45 lakh actually paid in FY26 (S1).

The RHP lists 21 delayed ROC filings between 2018 and 2026, all regularised with additional fees and with no penalties imposed. They include PAS-3 allotment returns for the fund's private placements filed up to 137 days late, the first auditor's ADT-1 filed 108 days late, and an MGT-14 filed 111 days late (S1). There were also repeated EPF and ESI payment delays, up to 60 days in FY26 at the Karni unit, TDS return delays of up to 46 days, and minor GST 3B delays (S1).

items: The RHP admits 'some approvals that were applicable earlier had not been procured at that time and are generally obtained as and when the Company becomes aware of such requirements' (S1).
Auditors have changed twice: A. Bothra & Co. (first auditor), then Abhishek V Jain & Co. (2021), now peer-reviewed GGPS and Associates. The statutory audit fee was Rs 1.50 lakh in FY26 (S1).
The only outstanding litigation is the Rs 276.84 lakh income-tax demand against the company. None is disclosed against promoters or directors (S1).

The RHP contains multiple internal inconsistencies across chapters in brand revenue, product revenue, channel revenue, customer concentration and inventory, which raises questions about diligence quality (S1).

blocks.text: No single item here is fraud-grade. Together they describe a promoter-run family business with thin independent oversight (board and CFO installed in 2025), parallel ventures and loose record-keeping (S1).

items: Inventory and cash conversion: inventory is 74.5% of FY26 revenue, packing stock covers more than five years of use, and three-year operating cash flow is Rs 22.63 lakh versus Rs 1,204.46 lakh PAT. Any write-down would hit profits directly (S1).

Demand-repayable debt: short-term borrowings of Rs 902.69 lakh at March 2026, rising to Rs 1,073.70 lakh by August 2026, are repayable on demand. Cash was Rs 2.35 lakh, and the company depends on the lender and the promoters' personal collateral (S1).
Brand and IP: three brands are 88.7% of revenue and the 'Vishal' marks are opposed. An adverse ruling could restrict use of a brand worth Rs 1,051.6 lakh of FY26 sales (S1).
Geographic and channel concentration: Rajasthan is 50.42% of revenue, and general trade (57.91%) runs without contracts or an order book (S1).
Tax demand of Rs 276.84 lakh, about 53% of FY26 PAT, is not provided for (S1).

blocks.text: Of these, the first two interact. A lender tightening the cash-credit line while inventory is this large would squeeze the business quickly. The IPO's debt repayment helps only until the line is re-drawn (S1).
The inventory and cash-conversion risk is the one that would most change an investor's decision. It goes to whether the reported profits are real economic earnings (S1).

items: Execution: the Bachhasar plant has no orders, no approvals applied for, ex-GST budgeting and a January 2028 start. The quotations lapse on December 19, 2026 (S1).
Promoter conflicts: parallel snack companies, including Bhujialalji, in which Bikaji holds 49%, plus rented promoter property for the head office, main unit and new plant (S1, S13).
Unlocked overhang: India Customer Insight Fund's 22.24% post-issue stake is free to sell from listing (S1).
Outsourced hand-made production: the Batara-Batari home-rolling model limits direct hygiene and quality control on the largest product line (S1).
SME liquidity: trading is through a single market maker on NSE Emerge with a minimum application of Rs 2.30 lakh, and the exit route can be thin (S1, S2).

blocks.text: On lock-in: the SME framework applied here locks only 20.23% of post-issue capital for three years, with the rest of the promoter stake released in halves after one and two years. That is shorter than a typical mainboard promoter lock-in, and the fund's 22.24% has no lock-in at all (S1).
Generic boilerplate in the RHP (climate, transporters, insurance, food-safety regulation) is real but applies to every food SME. It is not what separates this issue from others.

Management's stated plans are qualitative and all tied to the new plant. It says Bachhasar will be the hub for machine-made production. Khichiya will move there from the Karni unit, which will close, new 5-inch and 7-inch rice papads (Zhakaas) and mini machine-made papads (Rozana) will be launched, and the RHP says operating margins are 'projected to improve' as freight, job-work and rental costs fall (S1). It also names future lines (roasted papads, pre-mix flours and ready-to-cook snacks) and positions the plant for institutional, modern-retail and export demand (S1).

The company says it is scaling the Papadmalji D2C brand through promotion, but D2C revenue was only Rs 0.25 lakh in FY26 (S1). The IPO press release carried no management quotes on growth, and no investor call or interview with specific targets was found (S5, S6).

There is no quantified revenue, volume or margin guidance anywhere in the RHP or the IPO press coverage reviewed. Any growth number attached to this IPO is an outside estimate, not a management commitment (S1, S5).

Near-term, FY27 carries no new capacity. Growth has to come from modern trade and distributor expansion, which grew distributor-served outlets from 4,740 to 7,470 in FY26 even as revenue grew only 5.62% (S1). The plant adds khichiya capacity from FY28 at the earliest (S1). The organised papad segment's projected 10% growth is a reasonable ceiling for an average player (S12).

items: Upside if inventory normalises and releases cash, and khichiya volumes grow into the new plant (S1).
Downside if the 25% EBITDA margin proves unsustainable in a low-barrier category, or if inventory has to be written down (S1).
A cost-overrun risk on the plant of about Rs 133 lakh of unbudgeted GST, plus unquantified shifting costs (S1).

blocks.text: The outlook rests on a plant that will not produce until 2028 and on margins that cash flow has not yet confirmed. Treat any growth narrative accordingly (S1).

This report is written on September 29, 2026, the opening day, so subscription data is at best partial. When checked, Chittorgarh's subscription page stated that subscription information was 'not available at this time' (S3). IPOGuru showed 0x overall, time-stamped September 28, 2026, 9:05 PM, which is before bidding opened, with category data 'pending first exchange data' (S4). No category-wise (QIB / NII / individual) figures were available from any source reviewed, and none are implied here.

There is no anchor book, so there is no institutional price signal or anchor lock-in to note (S1). The QIB portion is just 32,000 shares, 1.2% of the net offer, so demand will be driven by individual and NII bids (S2). Grey market premium was reported at Rs 0 (0%) by IPO Premium's listing and was not quoted at all by IPOGuru. This is unofficial and not an investment signal either way (S16, S4).

Check the final-day (October 1) category-wise figures on NSE before drawing any conclusion. Even strong subscription would not address the cash-conversion and governance issues that drive this report's call.

method: Primary source: the full RHP dated September 23, 2026, downloaded from the company's website (S1). I read the offer structure, capital structure and lock-in, objects of the offer, risk factors, business chapter (brand, vertical, state and channel splits, capacity, distribution), industry overview, management, promoters and group entities, restated financial statements and notes (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, inventory and material-consumption notes, related parties, contingent liabilities, tax, ratios), and the MD&A KPIs. All financials are the RHP's restated figures in Rs lakh. Ratios labelled 'analyst calc.' are my arithmetic on those figures. The RHP has no papad-specific market data, so market size and competitors come from the 2022 Frost & Sullivan report filed for Bikaji Foods (S12) and a Lijjat profile (S14). Those figures are dated projections, not current measurements. Bhujialalji's link to Bikaji comes from Bikaji's 2023 exchange press release (S13). Issue logistics (lead manager, registrar, market maker, listing date) were cross-checked on Chittorgarh (S2) and the company's price-band press release (S5, S6, S15). Material gaps: (1) the RHP contains several internal inconsistencies (brand, product, channel and customer-concentration figures, and inventory), which I flag where relevant, using the business-chapter and restated-statement figures. (2) Secondary summaries (S7, S8, S9, S10) contain errors versus the RHP (exchange, revenue units, objects, fresh-issue share count), so they were used only for cross-reference. (3) Subscription data was not yet available when this was written on opening day (S3, S4). (4) No management interview or investor call with forward guidance was found. (5) Offer expenses and the GCP amount are left blank in the RHP. Per the brief, valuation (P/E, EV/EBITDA, peer multiples) is deliberately excluded.
